title: Internal Structure of the Equilateral Lattice Path Integral: Crystal Angular Momentum, Emergent Vector Ground State, and Symmetry Breaking by Confinement
description:
In a previous paper (doi:10.5281/zenodo.22178585) we showed that an equilateral triangular (1+1D) and hexagonal (2+1D) path-integral lattice with the single amplitude rule "direction change = iε" reproduces relativistic dispersion, exact isotropy, and the speed of light c = √3 from geometry alone. Here we analyse the internal structure of the physical propagating band of the same model, in 2+1D and in a natural 3+1D tetrahedral-octahedral extension.

In 2+1D the physical band is exactly 5-fold degenerate and decomposes under C6v as E1 ⊕ E2 ⊕ B, carrying crystal angular momenta m ∈ {±1, ±2, +3} modulo 6; the s-wave is excluded by a factor-6 spectral gap in the local coupling matrix. In 3+1D the band is exactly 11-fold degenerate and decomposes under Oh as Eg ⊕ T2g ⊕ T1u ⊕ T2u; the exclusion factor is 12. A general law follows: for N lightlike diagonal directions the band has dimension N−1 and the s-wave eigenvalue of the coupling matrix is 1+Niε. A numerical double-slit experiment shows that a free wave packet is 98% T1u (vector). A 3+1D box-state calculation with hard walls places T1u consistently lowest in energy, with the T1u–Eg gap following 1/L2 to within 2%. Vector physics emerges geometrically as the preferred ground state of the lattice.

The paper (LaTeX and PDF) is in papers/paper2_internal_structure.*; the repository also contains all simulation code and further investigations.
